name: Anthracyclines
rationale: First-line cytotoxic backbone for advanced disease, with an EMC-specific response record curated in the clinical registry. Recorded as the incumbent this census measures new options against.

name: Alkylating agents
rationale: Given in combination with an anthracycline in advanced disease; the registry curates the combination arm's outcome. Part of the incumbent arsenal rather than an unexplored class.

name: DNA minor-groove binders / fusion-TF displacers
rationale: The class is on the board twice over: as monotherapy and as an all-approved-drug combination on the fusion's own documented downstream axis.

name: Platinum agents
rationale: No EMC-specific evidence exists, and the class holds no standing in soft-tissue sarcoma generally, so there is neither a disease-level nor a class-level reason to carry it. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Antimetabolites
rationale: A sarcoma-wide later-line option with no EMC-specific series anywhere in the curated record. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Topoisomerase-I inhibitors
rationale: No EMC report and no sarcoma-class standing that would license a transfer. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Non-anthracycline topoisomerase-II inhibitors
rationale: Carries none of the anthracycline record that puts its sibling class in clinical use here, and no EMC observation exists. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Microtubule-stabilising agents
rationale: No EMC observation, and the mechanism is the most sharply mitosis-coupled in the cytotoxic set. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Microtubule-destabilising agents
rationale: Approved in a different sarcoma histology on a lineage-specific result that does not transfer to a fusion-driven myxoid tumour, and no EMC observation exists. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Hypoxia-activated prodrugs
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09, the same day it was registered: the cheapest observation this class was registered to await was taken, and it went against the premise. The reading and its limits are owned by the route's grade — see RT-HYPOXIA-PRODRUG. ⚠ This closes the class on the evidence available here, which is transcript-level and small; it is a de-prioritisation with a stated basis, not a proof of impossibility.
requires: a hypoxic fraction large enough to activate the prodrug
a reductase-competent tumour compartment
zero_dollar_next_step: Score a hypoxia signature across the two readable EMC expression series and the fourth SRA cohort, then read the sarcoma phase 3 record for why it failed and whether the failure was mechanism or patient selection.

name: Radiomimetic cytotoxics
rationale: The class survives clinically in germ-cell and lymphoma regimens on histology-specific grounds with no soft-tissue-sarcoma instance to transfer from.

name: Direct NR4A-family agonism
rationale: On the board and closed on direction of effect rather than on reach: the fusion is a gain-of-function transcriptional oncoprotein, so an agonist of it is a candidate for the wrong direction. The closure is filed as premise-corrigible with a watched revival trigger.

name: RXR heterodimer pharmacology
rationale: On the board and closed: the one solved pharmacology in this receptor family does not reach NR4A3, and the closure was re-verified in 2026 against a primary source rather than left as an assumption.

name: PPARγ agonists
rationale: On the board as a downstream-effector route, because the fusion transactivates this receptor's promoter. The unresolved question is the direction of the intervention, not whether the axis exists.

name: Selective oestrogen-receptor modulators and degraders
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 on REACH, not on mechanism. The class needs a hormone-responsive 5′ fusion partner to import a hormonal input, and the partner-frequency arithmetic says one is reported in a single EMC patient in the world literature and in none of the partner-genotyped cases the cited cohorts cover. The reading and its bounds are owned by RT-HORMONE-PARTNER. ⭐ The MECHANISM survives and is stated in that route's grade — what fails is the number of patients it could reach, which for an ultra-rare disease is the whole question. ⚠ A denominator drawn from targeted-assay genotyping is the stated limit; this is a de-prioritisation with a basis, not a proof.
requires: a hormone-receptor 5′ partner, which is a minority subset of an already ultra-rare disease
zero_dollar_next_step: Pool the published partner-frequency series already curated here to size the hormone-responsive subset, and state the arithmetic of how many patients a partner-directed option could reach.

name: Orphan nuclear-receptor agonism outside the NR4A family
rationale: A registered lane with no route. It targets the disease's actual clinical problem -- dormancy and late metastasis -- and it repoints the orphan-nuclear-receptor modelling stack built for NR4A3 onto a receptor that has a published tool compound, which is the known-answer control NR4A3 never had.
requires: expression of the receptor in EMC tissue
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the receptor in the targeted expression panel already committed here, then state whether the existing pocket-modelling pipeline runs unmodified on its ligand-binding domain.

name: Androgen-receptor antagonists and degraders
rationale: No androgen-receptor dependency is reported in EMC and none of the known 5′ partners is an androgen-responsive locus, so the partner-imports-an-input argument that keeps the oestrogen class alive has no instance here.

name: Aromatase inhibitors
rationale: Depletes a ligand for a receptor EMC has not been shown to depend on; the hormone-responsive-partner argument runs through the receptor itself rather than through circulating ligand.

name: GnRH analogues
rationale: Acts by suppressing gonadal steroid output for tumours whose growth depends on it, and no such dependency is reported in this disease.

name: Glucocorticoids
rationale: Used across oncology for supportive and anti-oedema indications rather than as antitumour therapy in solid sarcoma, and no EMC-directed antitumour rationale exists.

name: Retinoid differentiation therapy
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on structural grounds. That ruling stands and its reasoning is owned there.

name: Vitamin-D receptor agonists
rationale: No vitamin-D-receptor axis is reported in EMC, and the class has no sarcoma-level antitumour standing to transfer from.

name: VEGFR / multi-kinase antiangiogenic inhibitors
rationale: The best-evidenced systemic class in EMC and the reason the arsenal is not empty: several agents carry EMC-specific response and progression-free-survival records in the curated registry. Recorded as the incumbent, and its response heterogeneity by fusion partner is separately on the board.

name: Anti-VEGF antibodies and ligand traps
rationale: The antiangiogenic hypothesis in EMC is already carried by the multi-kinase inhibitors that hold its entire clinical record; a pure ligand-blocking format adds no new axis of evidence and has no EMC observation of its own.

name: RET-selective inhibitors
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 on EVIDENCE QUALITY and on ELIGIBILITY, not on a negative measurement. The class entered the census because this is the one kinase reported both expressed and ACTIVATED in this disease. Reading the source shows the activation claim is a single sentence in a paywalled abstract, about 'a limited set' of at most ten tumours, with no recoverable denominator and no assay attribution — and the approved selective agents are approved on a molecular state this disease is not reported to be in. The reading and its bounds are owned by RT-RET. ⚠ Nothing here says the receptor is inactive in EMC; it says nobody has measured it, which is a different and more useful statement.
requires: confirmation that RET activation is present in fusion-positive EMC tissue rather than in a single historical series
zero_dollar_next_step: Read RET and its ligand/co-receptor set across the two readable EMC expression series and the fourth cohort, and re-read the original activation report in full to establish what was measured and in how many tumours.

name: ALK / ROS1 inhibitors
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 by reading the screen the class was raised from. The class entered the census because an inhibitor of it was among the low-IC50 hits of the only published drug screen on a patient-derived model of this disease. Re-reading that screen shows two of its three hits belong to a DIFFERENT single class, which is already on the board — and the two kinases this row is named for cannot be read on either expression platform, so the hit is unattributable here in principle. The reading and its limits are owned by RT-ALK-HIT. ⚠ The unreadability is an INSTRUMENT statement and says nothing about whether either kinase is expressed in EMC; what closes the row is that the screen's own weight sits elsewhere, not a negative reading.
requires: attribution of the ex-vivo hit to a specific kinase
expression of that kinase in EMC tissue
zero_dollar_next_step: Re-read the committed drug-screen artifact for the full hit list and its controls, then read each of that agent's principal targets across the EMC expression cohorts to see which are present at all.

name: EGFR inhibitors
rationale: The repository's own differential expression read places EGFR below baseline in EMC with no selectivity signal, which was already decisive enough to close a separate modality that depended on it.

name: HER2-directed inhibitors
rationale: No amplification or over-expression is reported in EMC, and the genome is quiet and clonal -- the profile in which a receptor amplification would be conspicuous if present.

name: FGFR inhibitors
rationale: Requires an activating fusion, mutation or amplification to select patients, and EMC's rearrangement is at a different locus entirely with no reported FGFR lesion.

name: IGF-1R inhibitors
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on the trial record in the nearest fusion-sarcoma comparator. That ruling stands and its argument is owned there.

name: MET inhibitors
rationale: MET appears in the surfaceome candidate list as expressed rather than as selective, and no MET alteration or dependency is reported in EMC.

name: KIT / PDGFR inhibitors
rationale: The registry records a biomarker-restricted single-patient use with prolonged disease stability. Recorded as part of the incumbent arsenal at its true weight, which is one patient.

name: NTRK inhibitors
rationale: The tumour-agnostic approval is conditioned on an NTRK fusion. EMC's driver is a rearrangement of a different gene, so the agnostic indication does not reach it despite both being fusion-driven sarcomas -- a distinction worth stating because the shared word invites the wrong inference.

name: AXL inhibitors
rationale: No AXL dependency is reported in EMC, and the class's principal rationale is reversal of acquired resistance to a targeted agent this disease does not receive.

name: RAS / RAF / MEK / ERK inhibitors
rationale: The class selects on an activating MAPK lesion. EMC's genome is quiet and clonal with a single founding translocation and no reported MAPK driver, so there is no lesion to select on.

name: PI3K / AKT / mTOR inhibitors
rationale: The class has been tested broadly across soft-tissue sarcoma without establishing a histology this disease belongs to, and no PI3K-pathway lesion or dependency is reported in EMC.

name: JAK / STAT inhibitors
rationale: No JAK-STAT dependency is reported in EMC, and the class's solid-tumour rationale runs through inflammatory signalling that this tumour's cold, sparse infiltrate does not supply.

name: SRC-family and BTK inhibitors
rationale: Both act on signalling axes with no reported role in EMC; the BTK arm is a lymphoid-lineage class with no solid-sarcoma instance at all.

name: CDK4/6 inhibitors
rationale: Selects on a cell-cycle lesion -- CDKN2A loss, CDK4 amplification, an intact RB axis -- and none is reported in EMC's quiet genome. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Transcriptional CDK inhibition (CDK7, CDK9, CDK12/13)
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09, the same day it was registered: the cheapest observation this class was registered to await was taken, and it went against the premise. The reading and its limits are owned by the route's grade — see RT-TXN-CDK. ⚠ This closes the class on the evidence available here, which is transcript-level and small; it is a de-prioritisation with a stated basis, not a proof of impossibility.
requires: evidence that fusion-driven transcription is more CDK-dependent than the host cell's
zero_dollar_next_step: Run the same class-inheritance argument already built for the DNA-damage-response lane over the transcriptional CDKs, using the sarcoma dependency prior already committed here, and state honestly that it is a transfer with no EMC line in it.

name: DNA-damage-response kinase inhibition (ATR, CHK1, WEE1)
rationale: On the board as a split pair -- the computed in-silico assessment and the cell-panel ask -- and it is the portfolio's strongest example of a class-inheritance argument. The computed half graded weak, which the record now carries.

name: DNA-PK inhibition
rationale: A registered lane with no route. Its appeal is structural rather than pharmacological: there is curated experimental evidence of an interaction with NR4A3 itself, and acting through the protein's own regulation needs neither a ligand for the pocket nor an assembled ternary complex -- so it inherits none of the blockers that hold the induced-proximity family down.
requires: that the curated interaction is regulatory in the chimera and not only in the wild-type protein
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the curated interaction records and their underlying primary sources in full, and state whether any of them was measured on a fusion protein rather than on wild-type NR4A3.

name: SGK1 inhibition
rationale: A registered lane with no route: a druggable AGC kinase reported positive across a full small series of EMC tumours with an internal negative control, published two decades ago and never followed up by anyone.
requires: confirmation at the transcript level in an independent EMC cohort
zero_dollar_next_step: Read SGK1 across the two readable EMC expression series and the fourth cohort, which turns a single antibody-based series into two independent modalities of evidence at no cost.

name: Aurora kinase and PLK1 inhibitors
rationale: Mitotic kinases whose therapeutic index depends entirely on outpacing the host's proliferating compartments. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: CSF1R inhibitors
rationale: Approved in a sarcoma whose biology is a macrophage-recruiting autocrine loop. The repository's own reading is that translocation-associated sarcomas carry significantly lower macrophage counts than non-translocation sarcomas, so the compartment this class acts on is the one EMC's class has least of.

name: Immune-directed kinase inhibitors (HPK1, TBK1)
rationale: Designed to amplify an existing T-cell response. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: Proteasome inhibitors
rationale: On the board, and it carries the best ex-vivo evidence any agent has in EMC: the single high-sensitivity hit of a chemotherapeutic panel, validated in both patient-derived models.

name: Histone deacetylase inhibitors
rationale: On the board as an expression-lowering route and closed there on selectivity. ⚠ The closure was re-scoped in the 2026-08-06 audit: EMC ex-vivo hits for this class do exist, so what is closed is the fusion-SELECTIVITY claim and explicitly not the non-selective-activity question.

name: BET bromodomain inhibitors
rationale: On the board with its HDAC sibling, closed on a sarcoma-wide dependency prior showing no selectivity window rather than on an EMC measurement.

name: PARP inhibitors
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep, and notably in the inverted direction. That ruling stands.

name: POLθ inhibitors
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 and the rationale CORRECTED the same day. The class selects on a COMBINATION — alt-EJ high with homologous recombination low — and the combination is absent because the HR half is not down. ⚠ But one half IS present: the alt-EJ module is concordantly higher on both platforms with a flat NHEJ contrast. The first version of this row said neither half was present, which was wrong and would have understated the disease's repair phenotype in the paper that quoted it. The reading and its limits are owned by RT-POLQ. ⚠ The missing half is also the half a transcript read cannot properly see, since an HR defect is usually a mutation — so this is a weak exclusion, not a strong one.
requires: that the replication-stress premise the ATR lane rests on survives its own weak grade
zero_dollar_next_step: Extend the committed dependency-prior analysis to the microhomology-mediated end-joining genes, and report it beside the ATR assessment's weak grade rather than as a fresh claim.

name: IDH inhibitors
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep as a nominal name-match only. That ruling stands, and the sweep kept it precisely because the disease's name misleads.

name: EZH2 / PRC2 inhibitors
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09, the same day it was registered: the cheapest observation this class was registered to await was taken, and it went against the premise. The reading and its limits are owned by the route's grade — see RT-EZH2. ⚠ This closes the class on the evidence available here, which is transcript-level and small; it is a de-prioritisation with a stated basis, not a proof of impossibility.
requires: a chromatin-remodeller defect or PRC2 dependency in EMC, neither of which is reported
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the PRC2 and BAF subunit sets across the EMC expression cohorts on disk, and check the committed sarcoma dependency artifact for the same genes so the answer arrives beside the negative that is already recorded.

name: PRMT5 / MAT2A inhibitors (MTAP-deletion synthetic lethality)
rationale: ⭐ One of the few genuinely biomarker-selected synthetic-lethal classes in oncology, and its biomarker is a copy-number state nobody here has ever read in EMC. The question is cheap and binary, and it has simply never been asked.
requires: co-deletion of the MTAP locus, which is unmeasured in EMC
zero_dollar_next_step: Read MTAP and its neighbouring locus across every EMC expression series on disk plus the fourth cohort; deletion shows up as a floor-level transcript, so expression data answers a copy-number question well enough to triage it.

name: HSP90 and chaperone inhibitors
rationale: ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-08-09: the class name did surface here before, as a chemotype-promiscuity observation in a docking-decoy analysis, not as a chaperone-dependency hypothesis. What survives is the hypothesis — that a chimeric protein is disproportionately chaperone-dependent — which nothing here has stated. ⚠ The class carries a long clinical record of failure on toxicity that any assessment must lead with.
requires: evidence that the chimera is more chaperone-dependent than the wild-type proteins it is made from
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the chaperone-client literature for FET-family fusion proteins, and check whether the repository's own structural work on the chimera predicts an unstable or partially disordered interface at the junction.

name: DNA methyltransferase inhibitors
rationale: Hypomethylating agents have a coherent rationale in fusion-driven tumours with quiet genomes, but grading it needs EMC methylation data, and no methylation dataset for this disease is available to this program in any form.

name: LSD1 inhibitors
rationale: The class's solid-tumour rationale is lineage-specific to neuroendocrine differentiation, and EMC's reported neuroendocrine features are immunophenotypic rather than a lineage dependency.

name: Menin-MLL inhibitors
rationale: Selects on a specific leukaemic rearrangement class; the interaction it blocks has no reported role in soft-tissue sarcoma.

name: WRN helicase inhibitors
rationale: Selects on microsatellite instability. EMC's genome is quiet, clonal and stable -- the opposite of the state this class requires.

name: USP1 and KAT6 inhibitors
rationale: Both select on lesions defined in other diseases -- homologous-recombination deficiency and a hormone-receptor-positive breast context -- neither of which EMC has.

name: NAMPT and DHODH inhibitors
rationale: Both starve a biosynthetic pathway whose demand scales with division rate. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Glutaminase inhibitors
rationale: Ruled out with the wider metabolic sweep on 2026-08-07. That ruling stands.

name: Arginine deprivation
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09, the same day it was registered: the cheapest observation this class was registered to await was taken, and it went against the premise. The reading and its limits are owned by the route's grade — see RT-ARGININE. ⚠ This closes the class on the evidence available here, which is transcript-level and small; it is a de-prioritisation with a stated basis, not a proof of impossibility.
requires: silencing of the argininosuccinate synthase locus in EMC, which is unmeasured
zero_dollar_next_step: Read ASS1 across the two readable EMC expression series and the fourth cohort. A single transcript answers the selection question, and the class already has a sarcoma trial record to read the answer against.

name: Asparaginase
rationale: The same enzyme-silencing logic as arginine deprivation, but the sensitising defect is a lymphoid lineage property with no solid-sarcoma instance.

name: Ornithine decarboxylase inhibitors
rationale: Its oncology use is maintenance in a MYCN-driven paediatric tumour, and polyamine demand tracks proliferation. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Fatty-acid synthase inhibitors
rationale: Ruled out with the wider metabolic sweep on 2026-08-07. That ruling stands.

name: SHP2 allosteric inhibitors
rationale: An adaptor node downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases, used to deepen or rescue MAPK blockade. EMC has no MAPK lesion for it to be adjacent to.

name: Nuclear export (XPO1) inhibitors
rationale: Parked by the 2026-06-22 emerging-modalities scan. That ruling stands and its reasoning is owned there; it is recorded here so the class cannot be re-proposed as unexplored.

name: MDM2 / MDMX antagonists (p53 reactivation)
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09, the same day it was registered: the cheapest observation this class was registered to await was taken, and it went against the premise. The reading and its limits are owned by the route's grade — see RT-MDM2. ⚠ This closes the class on the evidence available here, which is transcript-level and small; it is a de-prioritisation with a stated basis, not a proof of impossibility.
requires: confirmation that TP53 is wild-type in EMC, which the quiet-genome sequencing implies but has not been read out directly here
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the committed whole-genome trio analysis for TP53 status and check the MDM2 locus in the EMC expression cohorts, so the selection question is answered from data already on disk.

name: BCL-2 inhibitors
rationale: On the board inside the proteasome-inhibitor route as a combination arm. ⚠ The record was corrected in the 2026-08-06 audit: what the primary source supports is combination activity, and monotherapy was explicitly negative.

name: MCL-1 and BCL-xL inhibitors
rationale: Follows directly from a result the repository already holds and never pursued: BCL-2 inhibition was inactive alone and active only in combination in patient-derived EMC models, which is the signature of dependence on a different anti-apoptotic family member. Nobody has asked which one.
requires: identification of which anti-apoptotic protein the models depend on
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the BCL-2 family across the EMC expression cohorts and re-read the committed ex-vivo screen artifacts for every BH3-mimetic in their panels.

name: IAP antagonists / SMAC mimetics
rationale: The mechanism converts inflammatory cytokine signalling into cell death, so it needs a primed inflammatory context to convert. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: Death-receptor agonists
rationale: A class with a long record of clinical inactivity across solid tumours and no EMC-specific sensitising feature reported.

name: RAS inhibitors
rationale: Every agent in the class targets a specific mutant allele, and EMC has no reported RAS mutation.

name: TEAD / YAP inhibitors
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on dependency evidence and on target identity, and flagged there as worth publishing as a negative. That ruling stands.

name: Wnt / β-catenin pathway inhibitors
rationale: Selects on a Wnt-pathway lesion, and none is reported in EMC's quiet genome.

name: γ-secretase inhibitors / Notch pathway
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep, which retained it only as a trial-design precedent. That ruling stands.

name: HIF-2α inhibitors
rationale: The class is built for constitutive HIF-2α stabilisation caused by a specific tumour-suppressor loss. A hypoxic microenvironment is a different thing from that lesion, and EMC has no report of it.

name: Stapled peptides and designed protein binders
rationale: The de-novo binder class was assessed in the technique-class table and not ranked as a route; the ruling there also covers the peptide format, since both fail on the same unsolved half. That ruling stands.

name: Macrocyclic small molecules for protein-protein interfaces
rationale: A chemotype that reaches interfaces conventional small molecules cannot, which is the right shape for this target -- and it runs into the same wall as every other route through this pocket: no ligand of any kind is known for it, and the free-energy methods that would rank one cannot resolve the needed margin.

name: Condensate-partitioning small molecules
rationale: Assessed in the technique-class table and not ranked, on the field's own statement about what remains unsolved. That ruling stands and it is filed there as a watch item.

name: PROTAC / bivalent degraders
rationale: The most-worked route in the portfolio and no longer its lead. ⛔ That is a demotion of standing, not of evidence: every result stands, and this family's limits are the best-characterised here precisely because of the effort.

name: Molecular glue degraders
rationale: On the board and parked: it removes design handles rather than adding them, against the same quantitative selectivity requirement.

name: AND-gate bivalent degraders (avidity coincidence detection)
rationale: On the board: an architecture that tries to buy selectivity from coincidence rather than from affinity, and is parked on the chemistry of its second arm.

name: RIPTAC — bind the tumour protein, poison an essential one
rationale: On the board. ⚠ Its record was corrected in the 2026-08-06 audit: on this target the bound protein is a domain the paralogues share, so partial selectivity is a liability here rather than a tolerance.

name: Transcriptional chemical inducers of proximity
rationale: On the board: spend the ligand on rewiring the fusion's output instead of on removing it. One free CPU run from re-grading, per its own record.

name: Fusion-selective ubiquitination at the transfer step
rationale: On the board: discriminate at the ubiquitin-transfer step rather than at binding.

name: RIBOTAC / RNase-recruiting small molecules
rationale: Assessed in the technique-class table and not ranked, and filed there as a reopening trigger rather than a route. That ruling stands.

name: LYTAC / lysosome-targeting chimeras
rationale: The mechanism routes extracellular and membrane proteins to the lysosome. The driver here is a nuclear transcription factor, so the class cannot reach it by construction.

name: Autophagy-targeting chimeras (AUTAC, ATTEC, AUTOTAC)
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on compartment grounds. That ruling stands.

name: DUBTAC / targeted protein stabilisation
rationale: Stabilises a protein rather than removing it. The driver is a gain-of-function oncoprotein, so the direction of effect is wrong -- the same reasoning that closed the approved NR4A3 agonist.

name: Phosphatase- and enzyme-recruiting chimeras
rationale: Extends induced proximity to post-translational marks other than ubiquitin, which is an interesting fit for a transcription factor whose activity is phosphorylation-regulated. It inherits this family's unsolved half exactly: no correctly assembled induced complex on this target has been produced by anyone.

name: TF-PROTAC (oligonucleotide-directed degradation of a transcription factor)
rationale: An elegant fit on its face -- the targeting arm is the DNA element the transcription factor binds, which sidesteps needing a pocket ligand. It fails on the same arithmetic that killed direct DNA-binding-domain targeting here: the chimera binds the same response elements as its paralogues, whose DNA-binding domains are near-identical, so the oligonucleotide arm cannot discriminate.

name: Gapmer antisense oligonucleotides
rationale: On the board as the portfolio's junction-directed route. ⚠ Its committed design panel is under retraction pending regeneration at the corrected junction, and nothing from it may be quoted until that runs.

name: siRNA and RNAi
rationale: Registered with the antisense route as the same junction-directed deliverable, differing in machinery rather than in what it discriminates on.

name: Intron-directed antisense against the fusion pre-mRNA
rationale: Proposed and refuted inside a single day on 2026-08-07, with the feasibility computed rather than argued. That ruling stands.

name: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides
rationale: A mechanistically distinct class from the gapmer route -- redirect splicing rather than degrade the transcript -- and it has never been named here. It fails on a fact the repository already established for a different modality: the splice acceptor at the junction is NR4A3-derived and identical in the wild-type transcript, so the sequence a splice-switching oligonucleotide must recognise is not fusion-unique.

name: Transcription-factor decoy oligonucleotides
rationale: Never named here, and it is the obvious idea for a DNA-binding driver: flood the cell with the response element so the transcription factor binds decoy instead of chromatin. It fails on the same arithmetic as direct DNA-binding-domain targeting -- the decoy competes for an element the paralogues bind equally well, so the reagent cannot tell the chimera from the normal proteins.

name: miRNA mimics and antagomirs
rationale: Acts on networks rather than on a sequence, so it forfeits the one discriminating feature this disease offers -- and no EMC miRNA profile exists to nominate a candidate from.

name: Aptamers
rationale: A folded oligonucleotide can in principle bind a protein surface no small molecule reaches, but the target is nuclear and aptamer delivery to an intracellular compartment is the unsolved half -- the same gate the antisense route waits on.

name: mRNA therapeutics (non-vaccine)
rationale: Delivering a coding message -- a dominant-negative, a suicide enzyme, a decoy protein -- is a real format with no EMC instance. It waits on the same tumour-delivery gate as every other oligonucleotide here, and the payload would still have to discriminate.

name: Small activating RNA and circular RNA therapeutics
rationale: Both are up-regulating or durability formats. The therapeutic direction needed against a gain-of-function driver is removal, so the class is pointed the wrong way.

name: CRISPR nuclease disruption of the genomic fusion
rationale: On the board and parked on delivery. The genomic breakpoint is the one truly tumour-exclusive feature available, which is why the route survives its own park.

name: Cas13 RNA-targeting knockdown
rationale: Registered with the nuclease route; it reads the fusion transcript rather than the locus, and waits on the same vector.

name: Base and prime editing
rationale: Distinct from the RNA-editing approach already ruled out here, and not covered by that ruling: a cytosine base editor can install a stop codon, which the RNA-editing chemistry cannot. It reaches the same wall from the other side -- it needs a vector that delivers to a disseminated solid tumour.

name: Epigenome editing (targeted transcriptional silencing)
rationale: Never named here, and worth stating rather than leaving unexamined. Silencing the fusion means silencing a promoter, and the promoter belongs to the 5′ partner -- a wild-type gene the normal cells carry and use. So the approach engages the wild-type locus by construction, on top of needing the same absent vector.

name: Trans-splicing ribozymes
rationale: On the board: couple a suicide gene to the fusion transcript's sequence. Parked on the vector and on the absence of a modern demonstration of the chemistry.

name: Fusion-responsive synthetic promoters
rationale: On the board and closed on biology rather than on delivery: EMC lacks the neomorphic DNA-binding element the technique depends on, which is the precise reason it is a harder case than the fusion sarcoma the method was built in.

name: AAV and lentiviral gene therapy
rationale: The delivery chassis three registered routes here already depend on, recorded as its own class so the dependency is visible as a modality gap and not only as a footnote on those routes.

name: Oncolytic viruses
rationale: Parked by the 2026-06-22 emerging-modalities scan. That ruling stands and is recorded here so the class cannot be re-proposed as unexplored.

name: Oncolytic and engineered bacteria
rationale: Graded honestly in the 2026-08-07 sweep and declined, with the niche fit acknowledged as real. That ruling stands.

name: Unconjugated monoclonal antibodies
rationale: The surfaceome screen returns no antigen that is both selectively enriched in EMC and restricted in normal tissue, so this class has no address to be pointed at. ⚠ That screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture mRNA and structurally cannot see glycans or stroma, so it bounds classic protein antigens and nothing wider. An unconjugated antibody also needs effector recruitment, which the cold infiltrate does not supply.
requires: a selective, surface-accessible antigen

name: Antibody-drug conjugates
rationale: On the board through the surface-antigen route. ⚠ The 2026-08-06 audit found that route's grade was correct for one of its two antigens and wrong for the other, which fails on a different axis; and a large stromal proteoglycan was never in the screen's seed set at all, so the conjugate format's best candidate address here has still not been assessed.
requires: a selective, internalising surface antigen — and the never-screened proteoglycan is the open candidate

name: T-cell-engaging bispecific antibodies
rationale: Registered with the surface-antigen route. It removes the need for a pre-existing T-cell response but not the need for an antigen, which is where this disease's gate is.

name: Soluble TCR bispecifics (ImmTAC)
rationale: On the board twice: against the fusion-junction peptide-HLA and against a cancer-testis antigen with a clinical-stage reagent. Both wait on the antigen rather than on the reagent.

name: Trispecific and multispecific engagers
rationale: Adds a costimulatory or second-targeting arm to the engager format. It changes the potency and the safety margin of an engagement, not the availability of something to engage. The surfaceome screen returns no antigen that is both selectively enriched in EMC and restricted in normal tissue, so this class has no address to be pointed at. ⚠ That screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture mRNA and structurally cannot see glycans or stroma, so it bounds classic protein antigens and nothing wider.

name: NK-cell engagers
rationale: Substitutes the effector population, which does not address the gate. The surfaceome screen returns no antigen that is both selectively enriched in EMC and restricted in normal tissue, so this class has no address to be pointed at. ⚠ That screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture mRNA and structurally cannot see glycans or stroma, so it bounds classic protein antigens and nothing wider.

name: Immunocytokines (tumour-targeted cytokine fusions)
rationale: ⭐ The one antibody format whose address is not a tumour-cell antigen. It targets an extracellular matrix epitope, and the matrix is EMC's defining compartment -- so the class routes around the exact instrument limitation the repository has already flagged, namely that its surfaceome screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture transcripts and structurally cannot see stroma. The class also has soft-tissue-sarcoma clinical experience specifically. ⚠ The payload is a cytokine, so a cold infiltrate remains a real objection to the immune arm even if the address holds.
requires: expression of the targeted matrix epitope in EMC stroma, which the existing screen could not have detected
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the fibronectin and tenascin splice-variant transcripts across the EMC expression cohorts on disk. They are matrix genes, so unlike a cell-surface antigen they are visible in bulk tumour data.

name: Radioimmunoconjugates
rationale: Swaps a cytotoxic payload for a radionuclide on the same targeting arm, so it inherits the antigen gate unchanged. Dose is delivered per cell but the tumour is dosed per unit volume, and EMC's matrix-dominated bulk gives it few cells per unit volume. This is the correction the repository already measured against the nearest histology when declining boron neutron capture, and it generalises to every per-volume-dosed modality rather than stopping at the one it was first written for.

name: Masked / conditionally activated antibodies
rationale: Widens the therapeutic margin of an antigen that is expressed in normal tissue too. It is a solution to a problem this disease has not reached, because no antigen has been established at all.

name: Non-immunoglobulin binding scaffolds
rationale: Nanobodies, DARPins and affibodies change size, penetration and manufacturing -- all real advantages in a matrix-dense tumour, and none of them an address. The surfaceome screen returns no antigen that is both selectively enriched in EMC and restricted in normal tissue, so this class has no address to be pointed at. ⚠ That screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture mRNA and structurally cannot see glycans or stroma, so it bounds classic protein antigens and nothing wider.

name: Antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on which step is actually blocking. That ruling stands and its argument is owned there.

name: Autologous CAR-T
rationale: On the board. It faces the antigen gate and, additionally, a cold and matrix-excluded tumour for the cells to traffic into.

name: Allogeneic / off-the-shelf CAR-T
rationale: Changes the manufacturing economics, which matters enormously for an ultra-rare disease, and changes nothing about the antigen. The surfaceome screen returns no antigen that is both selectively enriched in EMC and restricted in normal tissue, so this class has no address to be pointed at. ⚠ That screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture mRNA and structurally cannot see glycans or stroma, so it bounds classic protein antigens and nothing wider.

name: CAR-NK cells
rationale: Substitutes the effector to improve the safety profile; the gate is the antigen and the trafficking, both unchanged. The surfaceome screen returns no antigen that is both selectively enriched in EMC and restricted in normal tissue, so this class has no address to be pointed at. ⚠ That screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture mRNA and structurally cannot see glycans or stroma, so it bounds classic protein antigens and nothing wider.

name: CAR-macrophages
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep, and contradicted in the direction that matters. That ruling stands.

name: In vivo CAR-T
rationale: Ruled out as a modality in the 2026-08-07 sweep on a registry query; the sweep deliberately kept its economics argument and dropped the modality claim. That ruling stands.

name: TCR-engineered T cells
rationale: On the board against a cancer-testis antigen, ported from the sarcoma where the approach is approved. Downgraded on the repository's own finding that EMC is cancer-testis-antigen-low.

name: Ex-vivo transcription-factor modulation of a cell product
rationale: On the board, and structurally unusual: the NR4A family is acted on outside the patient as a manufacturing additive, so the paralogue-selectivity problem that blocks every in-patient route here does not arise.

name: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy
rationale: Parked by the 2026-06-22 emerging-modalities scan. That ruling stands.

name: γδ T cells, NKT cells and virus-specific T cells
rationale: Innate-like effectors proposed for tumours where conventional T cells fail. They still have to enter the tumour, and EMC's infiltrate is sparse and excluded by a dense matrix. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplant
rationale: A graft-versus-tumour strategy with no role in adult soft-tissue sarcoma and toxicity that an indolent disease could not justify.

name: Peptide and RNA cancer vaccines
rationale: On the board against the fusion junction, which is the disease's one genuinely tumour-exclusive epitope source. Parked on immunogenicity, which its own record states is not a computational question.

name: Shared / off-the-shelf tumour antigens
rationale: On the board as the antigen itself, shared by three delivery routes. ⚠ The upstream junction panel is under retraction, and the HLA coverage artifact computed from it inherits that defect.

name: DNA vaccines
rationale: A delivery variant of the same junction-epitope hypothesis already on the board, with weaker human immunogenicity data than the formats registered there. It adds a format, not an axis of evidence.

name: Dendritic-cell vaccines
rationale: Manufacturing-intensive per patient, which an ultra-rare disease can least support, and it presents the same epitopes the registered vaccine route already carries.

name: Whole-tumour-lysate and autologous cell vaccines
rationale: Relies on the tumour supplying a diverse antigen repertoire, and EMC's mutational burden is at the very bottom of the range. The repertoire it would present is close to the normal proteome.

name: In-situ vaccination (intratumoural priming)
rationale: The strategy is designed for cold tumours, which makes it look like a fit here -- and the fit fails for a specific reason worth recording. In-situ vaccination releases and adjuvants the antigens the tumour already has. EMC's problem is not that its antigens are poorly presented but that a genome this quiet generates very few of them, so releasing more of nothing does not help.

name: PD-1 / PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors
rationale: On the board in combination with an antiangiogenic inhibitor, which is where its only EMC evidence sits; the registry records no single-agent EMC cohort at all.

name: CTLA-4 inhibitors
rationale: Broadens an existing repertoire rather than creating one. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: LAG-3, TIGIT and TIM-3 inhibitors
rationale: Release brakes on T cells that have already recognised something. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: Costimulatory agonists (OX40, 4-1BB, GITR, CD40)
rationale: Amplify an ongoing response. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: Innate agonists (STING, TLR, RIG-I)
rationale: Explicitly designed to convert cold tumours, so it deserves a stated reason rather than a blanket one. Innate agonism supplies the danger signal and the priming context; it does not supply antigens, and a genome as quiet as EMC's is short of antigens rather than short of priming.

name: CD47-SIRPα and myeloid checkpoint inhibitors
rationale: Acts through macrophage phagocytosis, and the repository's own reading is that translocation-associated sarcomas carry significantly lower macrophage counts than non-translocation sarcomas -- so the effector compartment is depleted in exactly EMC's class.

name: Myeloid reprogramming (TREM2, MARCO and related)
rationale: Repolarises tumour macrophages toward an inflammatory phenotype. Same compartment problem as the myeloid checkpoints, plus it still requires a T-cell response to hand off to.

name: Systemic cytokine therapy (IL-2, IL-12, IL-15)
rationale: Expands lymphocytes systemically with dose-limiting toxicity and no tumour address. ⚠ The tumour-targeted form of the same payload is a separate row and does not share this verdict.

name: Interferon-α
rationale: The registry records case-report use in EMC. Recorded as part of the incumbent arsenal at its true weight, which is anecdote.

name: Adenosine-axis inhibitors (A2AR, CD73, CD39)
rationale: Relieves a suppressive metabolite brake on T cells that are present. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: IDO / TDO inhibitors
rationale: A suppression-relief class whose randomised record in an immune-hot disease was negative, applied here to a cold one. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: TGF-β pathway inhibitors
rationale: Proposed for immune-excluded tumours, which EMC is -- but the exclusion here is a physical chondroitin-sulfate gel rather than a TGF-β-driven fibroblast programme, and the repository's stromal sweep already declined the collagen-stiffening class on exactly that distinction.

name: Regulatory T-cell depletion
rationale: Removes suppression of an effector population that is sparse to begin with. EMC's measured microenvironment is immune-cold with a low mutational burden, which is the registered permanent blocker this class's mechanism runs directly into.

name: Fibroblast-activation-protein-directed agents
rationale: On the board as a radioligand route, and the 2026-08-07 sweep found a live alpha-emitter trial in relapsed sarcoma with a companion diagnostic. ⚠ The repository's own flat FAP reading came from a stroma-blind instrument, so it does not bound a stromal target.

name: Oncofetal chondroitin sulfate targeting
rationale: A registered lane with no route, and the best-argued matrix address the sweep found: it turns EMC's defining glycan into the target, and it belongs to an antigen class the surfaceome screen structurally could not have found because a sulfation pattern has no gene to rank.
requires: the oncofetal sulfation pattern in EMC tissue, which no committed artifact has measured
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the chondroitin-sulfate biosynthesis and sulfotransferase gene set in the targeted expression panel already committed here — the enzymes that build the epitope are genes even though the epitope is not.

name: Inhibition of tumour glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09, the same day it was registered: the cheapest observation this class was registered to await was taken, and it went against the premise. The reading and its limits are owned by the route's grade — see RT-MATRIX-SYNTHESIS. ⚠ This closes the class on the evidence available here, which is transcript-level and small; it is a de-prioritisation with a stated basis, not a proof of impossibility.
requires: that matrix production is load-bearing for the tumour rather than incidental to it
zero_dollar_next_step: Grade the chondroitin-sulfate and sulfate-donor pathway read that is ALREADY committed in the targeted expression panel — the data exists on disk and nobody has drawn a therapeutic conclusion from it.

name: Vascular-disrupting agents
rationale: Collapses established tumour vasculature, so its effect scales with how much vasculature there is, and EMC is reported hypovascular. The class is pointed at the compartment this tumour has least of.

name: Enzymatic matrix depletion
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on both enzyme specificity and the strategy's own randomised failure. That ruling stands.

name: Stromal normalisation (LOX / LOXL2, FAK, angiotensin axis)
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep, with a stated condition under which it would be revisited. That ruling stands.

name: Hyaluronan-receptor-directed agents
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep by the repository's own expression data. That ruling stands.

name: Integrin and matrix-metalloproteinase inhibitors
rationale: Both classes have large negative randomised records across solid tumours including sarcoma, and neither has an EMC-specific rationale that would distinguish this attempt from those.

name: Fasting-mimicking, ketogenic and amino-acid-restriction diets
rationale: The mechanism is differential stress resistance between fast-dividing tumour cells and normal tissue. The class couples its effect to proliferation rate, and EMC is a slow-cycling tumour with an indolent natural history -- the profile that makes a division-rate-dependent mechanism weakest, and the same ground on which a physical modality was already declined here.

name: Microbiome modulation
rationale: Its evidence base is modulation of checkpoint-inhibitor response, and checkpoint inhibition has no single-agent foothold in EMC to modulate.

name: β-emitting peptide receptor radioligand therapy
rationale: On the board as a neuroendocrine-receptor theranostic, where the cheapest possible confirmation has still not been done and the normal-tissue window is already computed as broad.

name: α-emitting radioligand therapy
rationale: Registered with the stromal radioligand route, where the 2026 increment is specifically an alpha-emitter trial in relapsed sarcoma. Dose is delivered per cell but the tumour is dosed per unit volume, and EMC's matrix-dominated bulk gives it few cells per unit volume. This is the correction the repository already measured against the nearest histology when declining boron neutron capture, and it generalises to every per-volume-dosed modality rather than stopping at the one it was first written for.

name: Auger-electron emitters
rationale: Requires nuclear-proximal delivery per cell to achieve its very short range, which is the most cell-count-dependent of all radionuclide classes. Dose is delivered per cell but the tumour is dosed per unit volume, and EMC's matrix-dominated bulk gives it few cells per unit volume. This is the correction the repository already measured against the nearest histology when declining boron neutron capture, and it generalises to every per-volume-dosed modality rather than stopping at the one it was first written for.

name: Radioembolization and arterial radionuclide delivery
rationale: Delivered through a hepatic arterial supply for liver-dominant disease, and EMC's metastatic pattern is lung-predominant.

name: External-beam radiotherapy
rationale: Part of the standard of care for close or threatened margins and for large or high-grade tumours. ⚠ Its actual benefit in this disease is contested in the repository's own record, which is a separate registered question.

name: Proton and carbon-ion therapy
rationale: Probed by the 2026-08-07 physical-modality sweep, which carries dedicated carbon-ion queries against both the literature and the trial registry. Searched without being ruled on.
requires: resolution of the existing radioresistance contradiction, which is itself a registered lane
zero_dollar_next_step: Fold this into the radioresistance reappraisal already scoped here: search the particle-therapy registries for myxoid and chondroid sarcoma histologies, which publish institutional series that a histology-level search reaches.

name: Brachytherapy
rationale: Already present in the radiotherapy dose reappraisal this repository holds. The route survives as an arm of that reappraisal; the novelty claim does not.
zero_dollar_next_step: Include brachytherapy arms when the radioresistance reappraisal's dose-response regression is built, rather than restricting it to external-beam series.

name: Radiosensitizers
rationale: Probed by the 2026-08-07 metabolism-and-strategy sweep. Searched without being ruled on.
requires: that the reported combination response is attributable to interaction rather than to either agent alone
zero_dollar_next_step: Re-read the combination case report in full and pool every EMC case in the literature where systemic therapy and radiotherapy were given concurrently, using the pooling method this repository already owns.

name: Boron neutron capture therapy
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on a measurement in the nearest histology. ⭐ That ruling's reasoning generalises well beyond it, and this census applies the same correction to several other per-volume-dosed classes.

name: FLASH ultra-high-dose-rate radiotherapy
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep and filed as a method-watch trigger. That ruling stands.

name: Radioprotectors
rationale: A normal-tissue toxicity intervention rather than an antitumour one; it changes the tolerable dose and nothing about the tumour.

name: Wide local excision and metastasectomy
rationale: The backbone of curative treatment, and metastasectomy remains legitimate in indolent metastatic disease. Recorded because a census of what reaches this disease that omitted its most effective intervention would misstate the baseline.

name: Observation and deferred intervention
rationale: Recorded as a treatment decision rather than an absence of one: the registry names it a legitimate option in indolent metastatic disease, which makes it the comparator any new systemic option has to beat.

name: Isolated limb perfusion
rationale: Probed by the 2026-08-07 physical-modality sweep, whose retrieval file carries a dedicated isolated-limb-perfusion-by-histology query. ⚠ The sweep's §6 table does not list it, so it was searched without being ruled on — which is why the route survives while the novelty claim does not.
requires: an extremity primary or extremity-confined recurrence
zero_dollar_next_step: Pool the anatomical-site distribution across the EMC series already curated in the clinical registry to size the eligible fraction, and search the perfusion literature for myxoid histologies specifically.

name: Isolated lung perfusion and regional pulmonary delivery
rationale: ⭐ EMC's metastatic pattern is lung-predominant and its course is indolent, which is the profile regional pulmonary delivery was developed for: high local exposure, contained toxicity, and time for it to matter. Never considered here.
requires: lung-limited metastatic disease
zero_dollar_next_step: Extract the metastatic-site distribution and time-to-metastasis already curated in the clinical registry, and state what fraction of patients are lung-limited and for how long.

name: Inhaled and aerosolised cytotoxic therapy
rationale: The same lung-predominant argument as regional perfusion, in a repeatable outpatient format rather than a surgical one -- which matters far more for a disease measured in years than in months.
requires: lung-limited or lung-dominant metastatic disease
zero_dollar_next_step: Assess it together with regional pulmonary delivery from the same registry extraction, since both are selected by the same patient feature.

name: Percutaneous ablation (radiofrequency, microwave, cryo, focused ultrasound)
rationale: Probed by the 2026-08-07 physical-modality sweep, which carries cryoablation, histotripsy and focused-ultrasound queries. Searched without being ruled on.
requires: oligometastatic disease, which the indolent course makes common
zero_dollar_next_step: Read metastatic burden at presentation from the curated registry cohorts and state what fraction would meet a conventional oligometastatic threshold.

name: Regional hyperthermia
rationale: Probed by the 2026-08-07 physical-modality sweep, which carries a dedicated regional-hyperthermia-in-soft-tissue-sarcoma query. Searched without being ruled on.
zero_dollar_next_step: Read the randomised sarcoma trial's histology breakdown for myxoid subtypes, and check whether its benefit tracked grade or proliferation index.

name: Tumour-treating fields
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on mechanism and on the absence of any sarcoma trial. That ruling stands.

name: Near-infrared photoimmunotherapy
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on the target of the only approved agent and on light penetration. That ruling stands.

name: Photodynamic therapy
rationale: Distinct from the photoimmunotherapy already ruled out here, and it fails on the half of that ruling that is about physics rather than about the antibody: light penetration is millimetres and EMC arises deep in proximal soft tissue.

name: Electrochemotherapy and electroporation
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on the depth limit in its own sarcoma trial. That ruling stands.

name: Intraperitoneal and intrathecal regional chemotherapy
rationale: Both compartments are selected by a metastatic pattern EMC does not have; its dissemination is haematogenous and lung-predominant.

name: Transarterial chemoembolization and hepatic arterial infusion
rationale: Selected by liver-dominant disease with an arterial supply to exploit; EMC's pattern is lung-predominant.

name: Bisphosphonates and RANKL inhibitors
rationale: Selected by skeletal metastasis, which is not EMC's dominant pattern; despite the name, this tumour is extraskeletal and disseminates to lung.

name: Repurposed non-oncology agents (metformin, statins, propranolol, antiparasitics, disulfiram)
rationale: A large class with a common shape: preclinical breadth, no biomarker, and no randomised solid-tumour confirmation. None has an EMC-specific hypothesis, and adopting any would spend the program's only scarce resource -- a collaborator's attention -- on a class with no way to be right for a stated reason.

name: COX-2 inhibitors and aspirin
rationale: Its rationale is inflammation-driven tumour promotion, and EMC's microenvironment is sparse and non-inflamed.

name: Senolytics and pro-senescence therapy
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on the disease's treatment history. That ruling stands and its argument is owned there.

name: Pharmacology borrowed from mucin-depositing non-cancer disease
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on driver biology. That ruling stands.

name: Endogenous retroviral and repeat-derived antigens
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep, and explicitly down-ranked for being unfalsifiable from the desk. That ruling stands.

name: Anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents
rationale: A supportive-care indication addressing thrombotic risk, with no antitumour claim to assess.

name: Nanoparticle, liposomal and albumin-bound formulations
rationale: Reformulation improves exposure and toxicity for an agent whose activity is already established. In EMC the limiting fact about the cytotoxic classes is that their activity is modest, not that their exposure is, so the class addresses the wrong half. ⚠ A matrix-dense tumour also penalises particle penetration specifically.

name: Polymer-drug conjugates
rationale: Relies on passive retention in leaky vasculature, and EMC is reported hypovascular -- the tumour property the effect depends on.

name: Lipid nanoparticles for oligonucleotide delivery
rationale: The formulation that would carry the portfolio's oligonucleotide routes to a solid tumour, recorded as a class so the gate is visible as a modality rather than only as those routes' footnote.

name: Extracellular-vesicle delivery
rationale: An alternative carrier for the same undelivered payloads, at an earlier stage of clinical maturity than the lipid formulations it would compete with.

name: Peptide-drug and small-molecule-drug conjugates
rationale: Substitutes a smaller targeting arm for an antibody, which improves penetration in dense tissue and changes nothing about what there is to target. The surfaceome screen returns no antigen that is both selectively enriched in EMC and restricted in normal tissue, so this class has no address to be pointed at. ⚠ That screen ranks tumour-cell monoculture mRNA and structurally cannot see glycans or stroma, so it bounds classic protein antigens and nothing wider.

name: Tumour-activated prodrugs (enzyme- and pH-triggered)
rationale: Requires a tumour-restricted activating condition. No such enzyme or gradient has been established in EMC. ⚠ The hypoxia-triggered form of this idea is a separate row and does not share this verdict, because hypoxia is a condition this tumour plausibly has.

name: Intratumoural depots and sustained-release implants
rationale: Solves local exposure for an accessible mass, and EMC's clinical problem is disseminated metastatic disease that a local depot does not reach.

name: Blood-brain-barrier-crossing delivery
rationale: Selected by central-nervous-system involvement, which is not a feature of EMC's metastatic pattern.

name: Adaptive and evolution-guided dosing
rationale: A registered lane with no route. It asks nothing new of chemistry and everything of scheduling, it costs nothing, and the sweep found EMC close to an ideal indication on several independent grounds. Its falsifier is itself a publishable question.
requires: a measurable marker to adapt on, in a disease whose response endpoint is itself contested
zero_dollar_next_step: Build the model on the pooled progression-free-survival data already curated here, and state the conditions under which adaptive scheduling would and would not beat continuous dosing.

name: Metronomic dosing
rationale: Probed by the 2026-08-07 metabolism-and-strategy sweep, which carries a metronomic and maintenance-therapy query scoped to sarcoma. Searched without being ruled on.
zero_dollar_next_step: Add it as the comparator arm when the adaptive-scheduling model is built, so the two scheduling hypotheses are evaluated against each other rather than each against continuous dosing alone.

name: Treatment sequencing and line ordering
rationale: ⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 on EVIDENCE BASE, not on plausibility. Optimal sequencing is a real clinical question in this disease and the published record cannot answer any form of it: no randomised evidence exists for any systemic therapy, every pooled denominator is under sixty patients worldwide ever, and the between-cohort response range is wide enough that this repository's own pooling REFUSES to emit a single all-regimen figure. The reading and its denominators are owned by RT-SEQUENCING. ⭐ The refusal is the contribution — this closes the class as an analysis target while making the negative itself publishable.
zero_dollar_next_step: Tabulate reported prior-therapy exposure against outcome across the curated cohorts and state what the published record can and cannot support about ordering.

name: Biomarker-defined basket eligibility
rationale: A registered lane with no route, and the sweep's finding is structural rather than scientific: an open trial defines eligibility by a fusion family EMC belongs to, while its listed conditions do not name the disease -- so no histology-based search reaches it. That is a reachability problem, and reachability is something a published paper can fix.
zero_dollar_next_step: Sweep the trial registries for eligibility criteria naming fusion families rather than histologies, and publish the resulting cross-walk as the deliverable.

name: Biomarker-stratified treatment selection
rationale: On the board: the 5′ fusion partner as a treatment-stratification variable. It is the portfolio's only route that changes practice without changing the drug.

name: Redefining the response endpoint
rationale: On the board, and upstream of most of this census: an indolent disease judged on a response endpoint built for aggressive ones will score every option here poorly regardless of what it does.

name: Expanded access, compassionate use and off-label registries
rationale: For a disease that will never have a randomised trial, the realistic route from a computational hypothesis to a treated patient runs through single-patient access and a registry that captures the outcome. The portfolio names publication as its endpoint everywhere and has never registered the mechanism by which a published hypothesis actually reaches a patient.
zero_dollar_next_step: Map the access pathways and the public outcome registries that accept off-label single-patient reports, and state which of this portfolio's candidates could in principle enter one.

name: N-of-1 and single-patient trial design
rationale: Probed by the 2026-08-07 sweep's ultra-rare trial-design query. That the census then excluded it on shared-driver grounds stands; the novelty claim does not.

name: Chronotherapy
rationale: Timing delivery to circadian rhythm optimises the tolerability of an agent with established activity, and this disease's problem is the activity rather than the tolerability.

name: Targeted covalent inhibitors and chemical probes
rationale: On the board, and demoted to a reagent rather than a drug: covalent engagement at a specific cysteine was the largest single demotion of the post-degrader ranking, and the instrument meant to license it fails its own positive control.

name: Direct small-molecule occupancy of a transcription-factor ligand-binding domain
rationale: On the board. It retires the ternary-geometry problem outright by recruiting nothing, and pays for that with a requirement nobody has sized: how much paralogue selectivity occupancy alone would need.

name: Ligands for low-complexity and prion-like domains
rationale: On the board and permanently closed: the domain is shared with the wild-type protein the fusion borrows it from, so a ligand defined by that feature cannot distinguish them.

name: DNA-binding-domain-directed small molecules
rationale: On the board and dead by arithmetic: the paralogues' DNA-binding domains are near-identical, far closer than their ligand-binding domains. This is the closure two other census rows inherit -- oligonucleotide-directed degradation and response-element decoys both fail on it.

name: Synthetic lethality and dependency-screen-derived targets
rationale: On the board through a chromatin-remodelling dependency. ⚠ Its prior came back negative, and the underlying screen contains no EMC line at all -- so the honest bound is not a small sample but no EMC observation.

name: Rational combination therapy
rationale: On the board as an all-approved-drug pairing on the fusion's own downstream axis. Recorded as a class because combination is a design decision in its own right, and because the repository has twice had to correct a combination result that had been read as a monotherapy one.

name: Programmable RNA base editing (ADAR recruitment)
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on the chemistry of the edit it can make. That ruling stands and its reasoning is owned there. ⚠ It does NOT cover DNA base and prime editing, which is a separate row with a different verdict, because that chemistry can make the edit this one cannot.

name: Individualised bespoke antisense programmes
rationale: Ruled out in the 2026-08-07 sweep on the published inclusion criterion of the programme concerned. That ruling stands. ⚠ It is a narrower ruling than it looks and does not reach the general access-pathway question, which is a separate row and is live.
